{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./vasp.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --nodes=1         -> -N 1
#   --ntasks=16       -> -n 16
#   --cpus-per-task=1 -> -c 1
#   -t 6:00:00        -> -t 6h
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 16 -c 1 -t 6h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: The Slurm header line `#SBATCH --job-name=2740#SBATCH -o out_%j.log` appears malformed/concatenated.
  # We do not translate job-name/output from that line.

  # NOTE: Slurm -o out_%j.log / -e err_%j.log use %j expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness yourself.

  # NOTE: Slurm --qos=hennig not translated.
  # Performance implication: job priority/time limits associated with the QoS will not be applied; scheduling behavior may change.

  # NOTE: Slurm --ntasks-per-socket=16 not translated.
  # Performance implication: without socket-level placement control, NUMA locality/performance may differ.

  # NOTE: Slurm --ntasks-per-node=16 not translated (already implied by -N 1 and -n 16).
  # Performance implication: none.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=1000mb not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a per-core memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm-specific $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR not available under Flux.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: may start in a different directory.
  cd "${PWD}"

  module purge
  module load intel/2019.1.144
  module load openmpi/4.0.1

  # Slurm used: srun --mpi=pmix_v3 ...
  # Flux equivalent: launch ranks under Flux. MPI wireup is handled by Flux/PMI.
  flux run -n 16 /home/joshuapaul/vasp_10-23-19_5.4.4/bin/vasp_stand > job.log

  echo Done
fi
"
}
